summary: Kingdomino plays fast and light: each turn you draft a domino and place it to grow a compact 5x5 kingdom, weighing terrain matches against crown-heavy tiles. It's a satisfying little optimization puzzle that resolves in well under half an hour, with almost no downtime.
praised: Extremely easy to teach and fast to play
Satisfying spatial puzzle for its weight
Great gateway/family game and works well with kids
High production value components (chunky wooden tiles in the deluxe edition)
criticised: Very light strategic depth, can feel too simple for gamers
Luck of the draw/tile order can swing outcomes
Limited long-term replayability for experienced gamers
Interaction is indirect and can feel solitaire-ish at low player counts

interaction.kind: indirect drafting/denial via turn order and tile choice

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: the winner is decided almost entirely by maximizing (territory size x crowns) across connected same-terrain regions
